subject: general
question: The cost price of a box of pen is ₹5,400. The shopkeeper gives a 62% discount on the cost price. What will be the selling price (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price × (100% − Discount%)

SP = 5400 × (100 − 62)%

SP = 5400 × 38%

SP = 54 × 38 = 2052

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,052.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) of the box of pens = ₹5,400

Discount offered on the Cost Price = 62%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × [(100 − Discount %) ÷ 100]

 
 CP = ₹5400 
• − 62% Discount SP = ? 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 5400 × [(100 − 62) ÷ 100]

⇒ SP = 5400 × (38 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 54 × 38

⇒ SP = 2052

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,052.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Discount and Marked Price

Generally, discount is calculated on the Marked Price (MP), but in this specific problem, the shopkeeper applies the discount directly on the Cost Price (CP).

Profit & Loss Basics

When the Selling Price is lower than the Cost Price, a loss is incurred. Loss = CP − SP, and the Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the equivalent single discount can be calculated using the formula: (a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100)%.
